details: The two-week US-Iran ceasefire is set to expire on Tuesday evening (April 21) in the US, with President Donald Trump warning of potential "bombs" if an agreement isn't reached and the Strait of Hormuz remains closed. Iran has denied reports of a peace plan involving uranium transfer and rejected a $20 billion frozen funds exchange. The US Navy reportedly seized an Iranian cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman, further escalating tensions. Oil prices have been volatile, and major European stock markets saw corrections due to the Strait of Hormuz situation. Bitcoin showed some recovery over the weekend, trading around $75,000, after breaking $78,000 on Friday, but crypto-related company shares were down amid increased risk aversion.
sourceName: Reuters (as cited by Investing.com and XTB)
title: Middle East Tensions Escalate as US-Iran Ceasefire Nears End, Impacting Oil and Crypto Markets

details: Despite the ongoing conflict involving Iran, China's economy has reportedly surpassed expectations. However, it continues to face challenges related to weak demand and structural risks. The broader economic fallout from the Iran war is affecting Gulf economies, with Turkiye actively trying to attract investors by promoting Istanbul as a regional financial hub.
title: China's Economy Navigates Iran War Fallout, Raises Questions for Global Markets

details: The BBC has identified a pattern of spikes in financial market trades occurring prior to public announcements made by President Trump.
title: BBC Reports Pattern of Trading Spikes Before Trump Announcements
